info.name: AISafe distributed
info.description: End-to-end tests of the distributed AISafe: every replica up, local access, forwarding between replicas, aggregation, catalogs, calls between services, the flight scheduling Saga, roles and failures. Select the environment "AISafe k3s" and run the folders in order (or the whole collection). See docs/postman/README.md.

item.name: 0. Setup: logins and every replica ready
item.description: Logs in with one user per role (the login virtual IP picks any of the 3 logins) and checks that the 3 replicas of each service are up. Run this folder first.

item.name: 1. Local access
item.description: Data held by the replica that is asked: answered locally, without asking its peers. The sample data is loaded by replica 0 of each service.

item.name: 2. Forwarding between replicas (peer-to-peer)
item.description: A record lives on the replica that created it (its home) and on the next one (its copy). A replica without it asks its peers, and the answer says which replica held it (X-Data-Node). The logs of the replica show each attempt: kubectl -n aisafe logs aircraft-maintenance-2 | grep forwarded

6. Flights: the scheduling Saga (flight-ops)
item.description:
Scheduling a flight is a Saga. flight-ops asks airports-routes for the route (C2) and aircraft-maintenance for the aircraft (C1), looks for overlapping flights on every replica, saves the flight as pending, and sends a copy of it to aircraft-maintenance (C4: reserves the aircraft) and to airports-routes (C5: confirms the route). When a step fails, the steps already done are undone (the aircraft's copy is canceled) and the flight ends canceled. All the calls go through the entry of flight-ops' own machine, under the same correlation id.

One flight is scheduled on each replica: every replica must then list all three. Each run uses an aircraft of its own, which stays: an aircraft with flights cannot be deleted, and flights cannot be canceled through the API.

8. Failures: with a replica down
item.description:
Stop a replica before running this folder, for example the one holding the copy of the sample data:

    kubectl -n aisafe delete pod aircraft-maintenance-1 airports-routes-1 flight-ops-1 --wait=false

or turn off its machine in Proxmox. The requests still succeed through the other replicas (the replica that does not answer appears in X-Unreachable-Peers). They also pass with every replica up.

item.name: 9. Cleanup
item.description: Deletes what this run created, so it can run again. The deletions are sent to replicas that do not hold the record: they forward them to one that does. The aircraft of folder 6 stays, with its flights: flights cannot be canceled through the API, and an aircraft with flights cannot be deleted.
